title: AMAT: staged Long after a 17.6% sell-off with no AMAT 8-K left it 14.6% below its $523 research target (12m)
call_reason: The published 12-month target of $494.60 is 10.7% above the $446.63 close, conviction is medium and the Sharpe gate passed, so the book takes 5 shares, staged around the October prints and FQ4.
one_liner: AMAT fell from $542.28 (Oct 5) to $446.63 (Oct 14) with no AMAT 8-K filing; since Sept 29 Micron, ASML and TSMC have all printed strong, and SEMI's 2028 WFE forecast is now $220B, which supports the $23.85 FY28 consensus. We buy 5 shares in tranches for a $494.60 target (research target (12m) $523), with a $328.23 stop just under the $335 thesis break.

thesis.point: The equipment upcycle runs through 2028, and it is being raised, not cut.
thesis.evidence: SEMI has WFE +21.8% in 2027 and raised its 2028 forecast to $220B from ~$200B on Sept 1, which supports consensus FY28 EPS of $23.85 on $55.9B of sales. Since our Sept 29 research, Micron printed record FQ4 revenue of $54.23B and guided FQ1 FY27 to $61.5B +/- $1.5B. ASML guided Q4 to EUR 14.2-15.2B and says planned 2027-28 supply will not fully meet customer demand. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to US$52.3-54.3B.

thesis.point: The market has already done much of the de-rating our research target (12m) assumes.
thesis.evidence: The close fell from $512.01 on Sept 29 to $446.63 on Oct 14, including -6.7% on Oct 13 (from $497.53) and -3.8% on Oct 14. AMAT filed no 8-K between Aug 27 and Oct 15. At $446.63 the stock is ~24.2x FY27 consensus EPS of $18.43, against ~27.8x at research ($512.01; derived). The research target (12m), derived, is NTM EPS of ~$22.8 (FY28 consensus less 4.5%) x 22.5x + $10.03 net cash = ~$522.5, rounded to $523, so the gap to the research target (12m) has widened from ~2% to 17.1%.

thesis.point: The next two quarters of earnings are visible, and the balance sheet is net cash.
thesis.evidence: The Q4 FY26 guide is revenue of $10.25B +/- $0.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $4.02 +/- $0.20. FY26 sales come to ~$34.3B (derived: 9M $24.04B + the $10.25B guide midpoint), and FY27 consensus is $46.3B (+35%, derived). Net cash is $7,957M ($10.03/share; derived from the 10-Q balance sheet). FQ3 converted 83% of non-GAAP net income to FCF (derived: $2,330M / $2,795M), against 51% over 9M (derived: $5,568M operating cash flow less $1,988M capex = $3,580M, over $6,980M), so the AR build reversing would add cash.

variant_view: There is no strong variant view against the Street. We are well below it: the StockAnalysis median target is $645.50 (40 analysts, Strong Buy, range $358-900) [10], and our recency-weighted median of the individual targets is $654.18 (result.json), while our $494.60 target and $523 research target (12m) assume the multiple compresses to ~22.5x NTM as the cycle ages. Morgan Stanley's cut to $563 from $642 (Sep 28) shows that compression starting [11]. Against the options market we are modestly more constructive: its distribution (result.json market_only) has a median of $442.00 and P(gain) 0.49, against our blended P(gain) of 0.57. Our research-only view is a median of $608.71. The edge is narrow. The options market prices the stock as if the cycle peaks soon, while customer prints since Sept 29 (Micron, ASML, TSMC) point the other way [12, 13, 14].

valuation.methods: [2, 3] Supervisor research target (12m) $523 (derived): Sep-2027 NTM EPS of ~$22.8 (FY28 consensus $23.85 less ~4.5%) x 22.5x = ~$512.5, plus $10.03/share net cash from the Q3 FY26 10-Q ($14,501M cash and investments less $6,544M debt = $7,957M, on 793.6M shares) = ~$522.5. Excluding the $2.42B of equity investments ($3.05/share) it would be ~$519.5. The five agents are at $507.03-517.03 (lead $515.03), using ~$8/share net cash. All blend forward P/E (21-23.5x on NTM/FY28 EPS of $21.5-23.85, i.e. 0-10% haircuts to consensus; one agent adds a 25x FY27 leg) and, for four agents, FCF yield (3.0-3.4% on NTM/FY28 FCF). The standard model's DCF leg gets 0 weight: its DCF check (runs/2026-09-29/AMAT/model_engine.json) flags it at ~$147-172, 67-72% below the other legs, because its 13.6% WACC is far above the ~5% that the multiples imply. The published target of $494.60 is the 12-month median of a blend that is 67% the options market and 33% the research view, so it sits below the research target (12m). Thesis break is $335 (~18x FY27 consensus).

catalysts.event: TSMC Q3 2026 earnings conference (results released; call 14:00 Taiwan time)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Taiwan was 22% of AMAT's FQ3 revenue, and TSMC's capex drives leading-edge foundry/logic tool demand. Q3 revenue (NT$1,494.24B) and the Q4 guide (US$52.3-54.3B) are out. Capex comments come on the call.
catalysts.watch: Whether the 2026 capex range of $60-64B is raised, and any first 2027 capex figure. Flat or 'disciplined' 2027 language would hurt.

catalysts.event: Lam Research September-quarter financial conference call (2:00 p.m. PDT)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Lam is the closest peer, with the same customers and the same WFE cycle. Its December guide and its 2027 WFE view are the market's first read on AMAT's FQ4 and FQ1.
catalysts.watch: The 2027 WFE growth figure, the memory share of the guide, China as % of revenue, and any comment on the Nov 10 Affiliates Rule date.

catalysts.date: 2026-10-28 (09:00 Seoul; evening of Oct 27 US time)
catalysts.event: SK hynix Q3 2026 earnings conference call
catalysts.why_it_moves: DRAM is ~26-29% of AMAT's Semiconductor Systems revenue, and HBM/DRAM capex plans drive the 2027 memory tool budget.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex level and any talk of slowing DRAM expansion to avoid overcapacity.

catalysts.why_it_moves: A peer read on 2027 WFE and on process-control intensity at the leading edge, reported in the same week as the memory prints.
catalysts.watch: The December-quarter guide and the 2027 WFE framing.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler quarterly reports and 2027 capex guides (Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon; they reported Oct 29-30 last year)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Doubts about AI spending, not AMAT news, drove the Aug 19 semicap sell-off, and hyperscaler 2027 capital plans are the most direct offset [19]. These capex guides set AI-capex sentiment for the group.
catalysts.watch: Whether 2027 capex guides rise again, or ROI and funding worries surface.

catalysts.event: BIS Affiliates (50%) Rule re-added to the EAR (suspension stayed until Nov 9, 2026, absent a future extension)
catalysts.why_it_moves: China is 28% of AMAT's FQ3 revenue. Reimposition would put Entity List controls on 50%-owned affiliates of listed Chinese customers. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US-China truce is extended to Jan 10, 2027, but no extension of this rule had appeared in the Federal Register as of Oct 14.
catalysts.watch: A Federal Register/BIS notice extending the stay, possibly to Jan 10, 2027. Without one by early November, expect the risk to be priced into the FQ4 guide.

catalysts.event: AMAT FQ4 FY26 results and FQ1 FY27 guide (the company has not announced the date; FQ4 FY25 was reported Nov 13, 2025)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first company read on FY27 against a consensus of $46.3B revenue and $18.43 EPS (+35% revenue), plus the China impact of the Affiliates Rule.
catalysts.watch: FQ4 against the $10.25B / $4.02 guide, the FQ1 guide, management's 2027 WFE framing, China % of revenue, FCF conversion (51% over 9M) and the AR build.

catalysts.event: SEMI year-end total equipment forecast (SEMI's forecast is bi-annual, with a year-end edition)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This updates the 2027 and 2028 WFE path that underpins FY28 consensus. It was last raised to $220B for 2028 in September.
catalysts.watch: 2028 WFE above or below $220B, and 2027 growth against +21.8%.

catalysts.event: Micron FQ1 FY27 results (FQ1 FY26 was reported Dec 17, 2025)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Micron is the biggest DRAM capex swing factor. It guided FQ1 revenue to $61.5B +/- $1.5B and says it is increasing manufacturing investment.
catalysts.watch: The FY27 capex figure and how much of it is tools rather than cleanroom construction.

catalysts.event: US-China trade truce deadline (extension announced by Treasury Secretary Bessent)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is a binary China-policy event. A lapse could bring back the tariffs the truce holds off, and the Affiliates Rule if its stay is extended only to this date.
catalysts.watch: Talks on a further extension in December. A lapse with no deal is negative for the 28% of revenue from China.

catalysts.event: TSMC Q4 2026 results and any first 2027 capex guide (Q4 2025 results were released Jan 15, 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The single most important 2027 tool-budget number for leading-edge logic, against 2026 capex of $60-64B.
catalysts.watch: A 2027 capex guide above the 2026 range supports the thesis. Flat or lower would point to a 2027-28 digestion.

catalysts.event: AMAT FQ1 FY27 results and FQ2 guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This confirms or breaks the +35% FY27 revenue consensus at the start of calendar 2027, after the China policy dates.
catalysts.watch: FQ2 guide run-rate against ~$11.6B/quarter of FY27 consensus (derived: $46.3B / 4), China revenue after Nov 10 / Jan 10, and gross margin.

risks.risk: AI or memory capex digestion: customers pause 2027-28 tool spending after the current build, and FY28 consensus ($23.85) gets cut the way out-year numbers are at cycle turns.
risks.signpost: TSMC's January 2027 capex guide at or below the 2026 $60-64B range, Lam's December guide down, or SK hynix/Micron talking about slower DRAM expansion. SEMI cutting 2028 below $220B in its year-end update.

risks.risk: China: the Affiliates Rule returns on Nov 10, 2026 (or after a Jan 10, 2027 truce lapse), hitting a region that is 28% of revenue. A suspended BIS denial order from the $252.5M settlement also remains.
risks.signpost: No Federal Register extension notice by early November. AMAT's FQ1 guide citing China, or China share falling well below 28%.

risks.risk: Multiple compression on sentiment: the stock fell 42.5% from $723.00 (Jun 30) to $415.38 (Sep 16), a stretch that included the record FQ3 and raised outlook (Aug 13), and 17.6% from $542.28 to $446.63 (Oct 5-14) with no AMAT 8-K filing.
risks.signpost: A close below the $415.38 September low with no fundamental cause. Below $335 (~18x FY27) the market is pricing a real downturn, which is the thesis break.

risks.risk: Cash conversion stays weak: 9M FCF was 51% of non-GAAP net income (derived) because of the AR build and facilities capex, against 83% in FQ3 (derived).
risks.signpost: FQ4 FCF conversion below ~70% or DSO rising again in the mid-November report.

trade.position: 5 sh (~$2,233, 9.3% of the $23,933 book; 10.6% of cash to deploy). The book-level Sharpe test sets the size; the supervisor's per-name 8% cap no longer applies, since the book dropped per-name caps on 2026-10-07. The loss at the stop is ~$592. AMAT would be ~54% of account risk, with 0.66 correlation to NVDA and 0.61 to AVGO already held.
trade.entry: The supervisor's 3-tranche plan over ~6 weeks. Its first triggers (Micron Sep 30, ASML Oct 14) are past and positive. Buy 2 sh after the TSMC call (Oct 15), 2 sh after Lam (Oct 21) if the 2027 WFE view holds, and the last 1 sh after AMAT FQ4 (mid-November, estimated).
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $328.23 stop (a noise floor of 2x one-month implied vol, just below the $335 thesis break), or on a close below $335 on fundamental news: customer capex cuts, an AMAT guide-down, or the Affiliates Rule reimposed with a quantified China loss. Take profit at $704.94. Reassess near the $523 research target (12m). No adds beyond 5 sh: the Sharpe test sets the size and AMAT would already be ~54% of account risk. Only a research refresh that raises the target, for example TSMC's 2027 capex above 2026 plus a strong FQ1 guide, would justify new sizing.

what_changes_our_mind: TSMC's 2027 capex guide (mid-Jan) at or below the 2026 $60-64B range, or Lam/AMAT guiding the December/January quarter down: that means the 2027-28 WFE path behind the $23.85 FY28 consensus is breaking.
The Affiliates Rule takes effect on Nov 10 with no Federal Register extension, and AMAT's FQ1 guide shows a China revenue hit well beyond today's 28% mix trend.

A close below the $415.38 September low that comes with estimate cuts rather than sentiment. Conversely, a fast move to the $523 research target (12m) without higher estimates would remove the edge and argue for trimming.
